title: Continuous-module presheaf actions and finite coordinates
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative topological ring, and work with profinite sets in a fixed universe large enough for its continuous-map groups [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Write $B(S)=C(S,R)$ with pointwise ring operations and precomposition restrictions. A sectionwise $B$-module presheaf means an abelian presheaf $P$ with a $B(S)$-module structure on each $P(S)$ such that $u^*(ax)=u^*(a)u^*(x)$ for every $u:T\to S$; its morphisms are natural additive maps linear over every $B(S)$. Let $M$ be an $R$-module with continuous addition, negation and scalar multiplication. Then $P_M(S)=C(S,M)$, with precomposition restrictions, is such a presheaf for the action $(ah)(s)=a(s)h(s)$. With $\otimes_p$ denoting objectwise $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$, this action is equivalently a natural abelian-presheaf morphism
$$\beta_M:B\otimes_pP_M\longrightarrow P_M,\qquad a\otimes h\longmapsto(s\mapsto a(s)h(s)).$$
For the pointwise multiplication $\mu^p$ of $B$ and unit $e^p(n)=n\cdot1$, it satisfies $\beta_M(e^p(n)\otimes h)=nh$ and $\beta_M(ab\otimes h)=\beta_M(a\otimes\beta_M(b\otimes h))$, as equalities of the corresponding tensor-presheaf morphisms after the usual unitors and associators. Postcomposition by continuous $R$-linear maps defines an additive functor to sectionwise $B$-module presheaves; in particular $P_f\beta_M=\beta_N(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes_pP_f)$ and it preserves identities, composition and sums. For every finite family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$, the module $\prod_iM_i$ with product topology has continuous operations, and the maps
$$P_{\prod_iM_i}(S)\longrightarrow\prod_iP_{M_i}(S),\quad h\longmapsto(\operatorname{pr}_i\circ h)_i,\qquad (h_i)_i\longmapsto(s\mapsto(h_i(s))_i)$$
are inverse natural $B(S)$-linear bijections. With their coordinate projections they exhibit $P_{\prod_iM_i}$ as a product of the $P_{M_i}$ in sectionwise $B$-module presheaves. The empty family gives the zero presheaf. For $M=R$ the presheaf is $B$ and $\beta_R=\mu^p$.

proof.text: We use the point-site and the pointwise ring presheaf $B(S)=C(S,R)$ specified by [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], forgetting its sheaf condition. Here are the continuity checks for the module-valued sections. If $v:X\to Y$ and $w:Y\to Z$ are continuous, $(wv)^{-1}(U)=v^{-1}(w^{-1}(U))$ is open for every open $U\subseteq Z$. If $v:X\to Y$ and $w:X\to Z$ are continuous, the inverse image of a basic rectangle under $(v,w)$ is $v^{-1}(U)\cap w^{-1}(V)$, so $(v,w)$ is continuous. Consequently $h+k=+\circ(h,k)$, $-h=(-)\circ h$, and $ah=\operatorname{act}\circ(a,h)$ are continuous for $h,k:S\to M$ and $a:S\to R$. The constant zero map is continuous. Thus all the stated pointwise operations are well-defined; no separation, compact-open topology on a mapping space, or discreteness of $M$ is used.

source.place: First two sentences: continuous linear coordinates and their inverse, before sheafification

proof.text: The abelian group and module axioms hold after evaluation at every $s\in S$, since they are the corresponding axioms in $M$. For example, $((a+b)h)(s)=(a(s)+b(s))h(s)=a(s)h(s)+b(s)h(s)$ and $((ab)h)(s)=a(s)(b(s)h(s))$; the other distributivity, unit and zero identities are evaluated the same way. For a continuous $u:T\to S$, define $u^*h=h\circ u$, which is continuous by step 1. It is additive and satisfies $(u^*(ah))(t)=a(u(t))h(u(t))=((u^*a)(u^*h))(t)$. Also $\mathrm{id}^*h=h$ and $v^*u^*h=h\circ u\circ v=(uv)^*h$. These are exactly the abelian-presheaf and semilinear restriction axioms in the statement.

source.place: First two sentences: continuous linear coordinates and their inverse, before sheafification

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] with scalar ring $\mathbf Z$, regarding abelian groups as $\mathbf Z$-modules. For abelian presheaves $A,P$, define $(A\otimes_pP)(S)=A(S)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}P(S)$. Along $u:T\to S$ its restriction is the unique additive map sending $a\otimes x$ to $u^*a\otimes u^*x$: the displayed pairing is additive in both variables, hence $\mathbf Z$-bilinear. Identities and composites have those formulas on each pure tensor, and therefore on every element, since pure tensors generate. The same construction defines $f\otimes_pg$ for natural additive maps $f,g$ by $a\otimes x\mapsto f(a)\otimes g(x)$. Naturality, identities and composition of these maps are checked on pure tensors by the same generation statement. This constructs the tensor presheaves and maps used below, without imposing a sheaf condition.

source.place: First two sentences: continuous linear coordinates and their inverse, before sheafification

proof.text: The pointwise pairing $B(S)\times P_M(S)\to P_M(S)$ is additive in both variables by step 2, so [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] supplies a unique additive map $\beta_{M,S}$ with $\beta_{M,S}(a\otimes h)(s)=a(s)h(s)$. This applies to ordinary algebraic tensor products: no continuity on a tensor product is requested. For $u:T\to S$, the maps $u^*\beta_{M,S}$ and $\beta_{M,T}(u^*\otimes u^*)$ agree on $a\otimes h$, since their values at $t$ are both $a(u(t))h(u(t))$. Pure-tensor generation makes them equal. Thus the section maps assemble to the asserted natural abelian-presheaf morphism.

source.place: First two sentences: continuous linear coordinates and their inverse, before sheafification

proof.text: For clarity, the usual tensor constraints in the statement have the following formulas on sections. The unit presheaf is constant $\mathbf Z$, the left unitor sends $n\otimes h$ to $nh$ with inverse $h\mapsto1\otimes h$, and the associator sends $(a\otimes b)\otimes h$ to $a\otimes(b\otimes h)$, with inverse given by reverse bracketing. Applying the universal property of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] in each variable defines these maps, since the formulas are $\mathbf Z$-multilinear. Their composites are identities on generators and hence everywhere; they commute with restrictions by their formulas on generators. Likewise $e^p_S:\mathbf Z\to B(S)$ sends $n$ to the constant function $n1_R$, and $\mu^p_S$ is induced by the biadditive pairing $(a,b)\mapsto ab$. These are natural maps by evaluation and pure-tensor generation.

source.place: First two sentences: continuous linear coordinates and their inverse, before sheafification

proof.text: On $n\otimes h$, the composite $\beta_M(e^p\otimes\mathrm{id})$ evaluates at $s$ to $(n1_R)h(s)=nh(s)$, which is the unitor formula in step 5. On $(a\otimes b)\otimes h$, the two associative-action composites evaluate to $(a(s)b(s))h(s)$ and $a(s)(b(s)h(s))$, equal by the module axiom. The iterated pure tensors generate the iterated tensor products by applying the generation assertion of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] twice. These checks therefore establish the unit and associativity equalities as equalities of tensor-presheaf morphisms, with precisely the associator and unitor specified in step 5.

source.place: First two sentences: continuous linear coordinates and their inverse, before sheafification

proof.text: This also explains the word “equivalently”. Given such a natural additive tensor action satisfying the unit and associativity identities, set $ax=\beta_S(a\otimes x)$. The tensor pairing and the additivity of $\beta_S$ give both distributivity identities; its unit identity at $n=1$ gives $1x=x$, and associativity gives $(ab)x=a(bx)$. These are the module axioms. Its naturality gives $u^*(ax)=u^*a\,u^*x$. Conversely, any sectionwise module action with that restriction law gives the tensor map by step 4 and its two identities by step 6. The constructions are inverse, since their values agree on every $a\otimes x$, which determines the additive tensor map by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: First two sentences: continuous linear coordinates and their inverse, before sheafification

proof.text: Let $f:M\to N$ be continuous and $R$-linear. Define $P_f(S)(h)=f\circ h$, continuous by step 1. At $s$ it satisfies $f(h(s)+k(s))=f(h(s))+f(k(s))$ and $f(a(s)h(s))=a(s)f(h(s))$, so it is additive and $B(S)$-linear. Naturality is the identity $f\circ(h\circ u)=(f\circ h)\circ u$. The maps for identities and composites have respectively the values $h(s)$ and $g(f(h(s)))$. The sum of continuous linear maps is continuous by the pairing and composition checks in step 1, and $P_{f+g}(h)(s)=f(h(s))+g(h(s))=(P_f+P_g)(h)(s)$. Thus the construction is an additive functor. Finally $P_f\beta_M$ and $\beta_N(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes_pP_f)$ both send $a\otimes h$ to $s\mapsto a(s)f(h(s))$, hence agree by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: First two sentences: continuous linear coordinates and their inverse, before sheafification

proof.text: Give $L=\prod_{i\in I}M_i$ its coordinatewise $R$-module operations and product topology. A map $q:X\to L$ is continuous exactly when every $\operatorname{pr}_iq$ is continuous: necessity follows because the projections pull opens back to open cylinders; for sufficiency the inverse image of the subbasic open cylinder $\operatorname{pr}_i^{-1}(U)$ is $(\operatorname{pr}_iq)^{-1}(U)$, and inverse images preserve arbitrary unions and finite intersections. Apply this criterion to addition, negation and the action on $L$. Their $i$th coordinates are $(x,y)\mapsto x_i+y_i$, $x\mapsto-x_i$, and $(r,x)\mapsto rx_i$. Each is a continuous operation on $M_i$ composed with the continuous projections and pairings of step 1. Thus $L$ has all the required continuous operations. This argument works for the stated finite $I$, including $I=\varnothing$.

source.place: First two sentences: continuous linear coordinates and their inverse, before sheafification

proof.text: The coordinate-continuity criterion of step 9 proves that $\Psi_S((h_i)_i)(s)=(h_i(s))_i$ is continuous; conversely the components of every $h:S\to L$ are continuous. The displayed forward map $\Phi_S(h)=(\operatorname{pr}_ih)_i$ and $\Psi_S$ are inverse because their composites evaluated at each $i,s$ are $h(s)_i$ and $h_i(s)$. They are additive and $B(S)$-linear: their $i$th coordinates on $h+k$ and $ah$ are $h_i+k_i$ and $ah_i$. For $u:T\to S$, both orders of restriction and $\Phi$ send $h$ to $(t\mapsto h(u(t))_i)_i$; both orders with $\Psi$ send $(h_i)$ to $t\mapsto(h_i(u(t)))_i$. Thus these are the specified inverse natural linear bijections.

source.place: First two sentences: continuous linear coordinates and their inverse, before sheafification

proof.text: The coordinate projections $L\to M_i$ are continuous and $R$-linear, so step 8 makes their postcompositions morphisms $P_L\to P_{M_i}$. To check the product universal property in the specified category, let $Q$ be any sectionwise $B$-module presheaf and let $q_i:Q\to P_{M_i}$ be morphisms. Define $q_S(x)=\Psi_S((q_{i,S}(x))_i)$. It is additive and $B(S)$-linear by step 10. For $u:T\to S$, its $i$th coordinate on $u^*x$ is $q_{i,T}(u^*x)=u^*q_{i,S}(x)$, which proves naturality. Its composite with the $i$th projection is $q_i$. Any other cone factor has these same coordinates on every $x$, hence is equal to $q$. This proves the product assertion directly, rather than assuming a limit-creation theorem.

source.place: First two sentences: continuous linear coordinates and their inverse, before sheafification

proof.text: For the empty family, $L$ has one element, its zero. There is exactly one continuous map $S\to L$ for every $S$, so $P_L(S)$ is the zero group with its unique scalar action. This is the zero presheaf (the same conclusion holds for each $P_M(\varnothing)$). For $M=R$ with its regular module structure, $P_R(S)=C(S,R)=B(S)$ with identical restrictions and operations. The pairing defining $\beta_R$ is $(a,h)\mapsto ah$, exactly the pairing defining $\mu^p$. Their equality follows from uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] at each $S$ and hence as natural transformations.
